key_figures: Harbormaster Ilsa Vane — takes bribes in fresh water, which is worth more than gold since the wells went brackish.
Sahuagin defector called Ssketh — begs sanctuary in a rain barrel, claims the Deep Maw is eating its own priest caste.
Tidecaller Wren — a drowned-god priestess who reads the future in flotsam; her prophecies always cost someone a finger.
Captain Harlow — smuggler queen of the Drowned Rat; runs blackwater gin and escaped debtors through the reef at night.
The Salt Abbess — runs a hospice where the dying are pickled alive "for the lean years"; half the city fears her, half owes her.
Bosun Cobb — lost his crew to sahuagin nets, now hires landsmen for "revenge voyages" that never return.
Mirella the Eel — fence for drowned jewelry; can tell which corpses wore it by smell alone.
Father Drown — street preacher who baptizes converts by holding them under harbor water until they stop struggling.
Scribe Pell — keeps the official drowning registry; for a fee, the drowned stay "alive" and their widows keep the pensions.
Knife-Jaw Joren — pit fighter with sahuagin teeth sewn into his gums; undefeated, possibly no longer entirely human.
The Lamplighter — tends the reef beacons; the only man the sahuagin won't take, and nobody knows why.
Widow Salt — brews brine-poison for assassinations; each batch named after the husband it avenged.
Quartermaster Voss — sells imperial weapons out the back of the garrison; checks every coin by biting it twice.
Little Fen — nine-year-old pickpocket who claims she can hold her breath for an hour; the guild is testing the claim.
Anatomist Dr. Morwain — pays in silver for sahuagin corpses, in gold for live ones; her cellar stairs go down past the waterline.
factions: The Blackwater Compact — Harlow's smuggler syndicate; owns the night reef and rents to anyone the Empire won't.
The Drowned Choir — the Maw's Voice's captive congregation; sings the surrender terms whether it wills or no.
The Brine Sisters — Salt Abbess's hospice order; pickles, prays, and keeps the inventory ledgers Sarella stole.
The Imperial Garrison — holds the tide-gates and the bridge; underpaid, undermanned, and selling its own armory.
notes: The east tide-gate's blessing lapsed three nights running — Brack swears he spoke it, the gate-wardens swear he didn't, and the lower wards have taken water each time. The Cistern King has tripled the freshwater price and blames imperial neglect; Voss is quietly selling gate-iron as scrap.
places: The Rotting Pier — lower docks built on drowned tenements; at low tide you can hear the old city through the planks.
The Brine Chapel — salt-stained chapel in the pier pilings where Tidecaller Wren reads flotsam; entry costs a secret.
The Drowned Rat (tavern) — smugglers' den in a half-sunk hulk; the floor tilts with the tide and so do the deals.
The Salt Abbey hospice — whitewashed walls, vinegar smell, and ledgers that list the living as stores.
The Old Reservoir — freshwater fortress of the Cistern King; the last clean water in the city, guarded by the thirsty.
The Reef Beacons — lamplighter-tended lights marking the safe channel; one beacon shines black at new moon.
